prompt:
I keep seeing this pattern in our codebase: type ApiResponse<T> = { data: T; loading: boolean; error: string | null }. What does the <T> mean here and why would I use a generic type instead of just defining separate types for each API response? Can you give me a simple example of when this is useful?

Give your whole answer in your reply; do not create or change any files. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, list your assumptions in your final message, and finish the work.

rubric.criterion: The reply explains what the <T> syntax means in the context of the provided type definition.
The reply explains why a generic type is useful instead of defining separate types for each response.
The reply provides a simple example demonstrating the usefulness of the generic type.
The reply stays focused on the user's question without introducing unrelated topics.
The reply avoids unnecessary scoring schemes, long reports, or unrequested deliverables.
